title: A class reference in echo or concatenation panics the compiler.
text: `class<Animal> $b = 'Animal' as class<Animal>; echo $b;` and `"a " . $b` pass `nvs_types::check_program`, and then `nvs run` panics in lowering with "a `ClassDesc` operand reached the implicit `string` conversion" (`lower/expr.rs:1146`). The arm's comment says `Ty::ClassDesc` is never a source expression's type, but a `class<T>` variable is one. `$b as string` compiles and prints the class name. It closes when the two agree: either `require_stringable` refuses a `class<T>` operand with a diagnostic naming `as string`, or the lowering converts it as `as string` does, with a conformance case for `echo` and for `.`.
